newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling loses marginally vs dollar, pound.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling loses marginally vs dollar, pound.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling opened weaker against the dollar and pound on Wednesday but by mid-morning was poised to strengthen on inflows from agricultural exporters, dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 55.49 against the dollar from 55.35 on Tuesday. Against the pound, it was posted at a mean rate of 90.57 from 89.90.
"After the shilling reached the 56 level, importer demand fizzled out. A lot of them decided to pull out because they found it too expensive to buy at that rate," a dealer said.
They said the shilling was trading at the 54.90/55.35 level and revived selling interest from exporters could help it to recoup losses against the dollar.

They were quick to add that the market was still very volatile. "There's a lot of speculation amongst investors which is the main reason the shilling is fluctuating between 53 and 56 (against the dollar)," another dealer said.
The money market was liquid with overnight rates quoted at 10-13 percent levels compared to 13-20 percent on Tuesday.
